issues.legal_issue: An offence under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act provision at issue requires the alleged insult or intimidation to occur in a place within public view, with a member of the public present.

An insult or intimidation attracts the provision only when it is directed at a person because of that person’s caste or tribe, and the charge-sheet must set out the alleged utterances sufficiently to permit the court to assess whether the offence is made out.
The allegations and material concerning the complainant’s injuries were insufficient to justify continuation of the prosecution for voluntarily causing hurt.

Abuse alone does not constitute intentional insult under the relevant provision unless it is of a degree intended or known to be likely to provoke a breach of public peace or commission of another offence.
